method_source: GraphRAG-style Local Evidence Aggregation: deterministic graph-window retrieval with the SA-MCGS local evidence schema, without relation-first memory, critical-pair revisiting, OC/core signals, or dynamic-core replacement.
deterministic_window_policy: one center node plus deterministic graph neighbors; fill by SCC order

conflicts.description: Bidirectional references suggest a failure in the document segmentation or relationship extraction process, as these clauses are logically distinct.

Potential conflict between the restrictive covenant on IP encumbrance and the general limitation of liability/warranty disclaimers if an encumbrance is required for compliance or liability mitigation.
The restrictive covenant against liens in 11.4.3 is rendered extremely rigid by the lack of cure rights in the event of a bankruptcy-related default.
The restrictive covenant on assets in 11.4.3 creates an immediate operative conflict with the liability/warranty framework in 11, specifically regarding default and acceleration rights.
Circular dependency between 'Effects of Expiration' and 'Annual Royalty Update' creates ambiguity regarding which clause governs the other during contract termination.
Conflict between restrictive covenant (11.4.3) and insolvency/default provisions (13.2) regarding the availability of cure rights and the automatic nature of payment acceleration.
Potential conflict between price adjustment overrides and fixed purchase targets, lacking a defined mechanism to adjust royalties (13.3.7) accordingly.
The restrictive covenant imposes immediate, non-curable material default status on payment paths that are otherwise treated as conditional, creating a severe conflict in enforcement logic.
The payment obligation for development costs (1.19) is rendered highly volatile by the absolute prohibition on liens (11.4.3), which triggers immediate material default and loss of cure rights.
The dense circular reference pattern between these nodes suggests a lack of clear hierarchy between general cost definitions and specific development cost line items.

Clause 9 mandates an unconditional payment duty, while 11.4.3 introduces a conditional approval requirement. The latter explicitly notes that any mismatch results in immediate material default and loss of cure rights.
Circular dependency between price adjustment (5.2) and purchase targets (7.2) creates potential for conflicting financial obligations.
The circular dependency between payment obligations and expiration effects makes it unclear which clause takes precedence regarding post-termination payments.

The bidirectional reference between a confidentiality destruction clause and a failure-to-supply clause indicates a lack of clear separation between operational performance terms and administrative/legal boilerplate.
Potential tension between the specific non-prohibition of third-party Beacon usage (6.2) and the broad intellectual property encumbrance restriction (11.2).
Circular reference loop between purchase targets and royalty updates prevents clear determination of which financial clause takes precedence.
Clause 8.2 depends on the content of 1.25, which is currently redacted/missing, preventing verification of ownership scope.
The restrictive covenant in 11.4.3 creates a high-risk dependency on the grant in 9.2, where any encumbrance on IP triggers immediate acceleration and loss of cure rights.
